newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coalition, SPD positions ahead of German tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Coalition, SPD positions ahead of German tax talks.

text.p: Following is a guide to where Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government and opposition Social Democrats (SPD) stood on Friday ahead of a second round of talks sweeping German tax reforms.
The two sides held a rare tax "summit" on Monday and a working group of six negotiators meets again at 1000 GMT. The coalition has set an Easter deadline for finding a compromise:
Cut top rate to 39 pct (vs 53 pct) Opposes big cut
Cut bottom rate to 15 pct (vs 26) Cut to under 20 pct
Cut on retained profits to 35 pct Agrees (vs 47 pct)
Cut on distributed profits to 25 Opposes, wants unified
Lower solidarity surcharge revenue Not subject to SPD okay

NOTE - Coalition plans to cut the 7.5 percent solidarity income tax surcharge in 1998 by two points, causing a revenue fall of 7.5 billion marks. This does not require SPD support to take effect.
